reasoning: Both attempts are correct: both mount once, bind the highlight to a source, clean up BlockTypeChanged, avoid yields inside Vide scopes and fit phones. B edges ahead on the tile-component criterion because its slot takes IsSelected and Select props. It also removes the ScreenGui when unmounted, updates the selection immediately on tap, and binds key-hint visibility to the input type. A is leaner and matches the project's style better, but it hardwires BlockPlacer into Slot and leaves the gui parented after unmount. B's needless restyle of Main and its extra Screen module cost it a little, but not enough to lose.

criteria.criterion: Vide, mounted once, components inside mount
criteria.note: `Hotbar` builds everything and is passed to `Vide.mount` once from Main.client.luau.
`isSelected()` reads the `selected` source inside BackgroundColor3, stroke Color and Thickness functions, which BlockTypeChanged updates.
`cleanup(function() connection:Disconnect() end)` runs right after connecting BlockTypeChanged.
One `Slot(props)` is built in a loop over BlockTypes.List, but it calls BlockPlacer.setBlockType directly instead of taking a select callback prop.
`slotSize` clamps 13% of the screen's short side to 44-68 px, about 48 px and 276 px wide on a 375 px-tall phone, centred clear of the thumbstick and jump button, with DeviceSafeInsets.
Clean, small diff that matches the project's style and passes all checks; the unmount leaves the ScreenGui parented and the key hint reads KeyboardEnabled only once.

criteria.criterion: Vide, mounted once, components inside mount
criteria.note: `hotbarScreen` is passed to `mount` once from Main; the Screen module's top-level sources are a shared store, not components.
`IsSelected` reads `read(props.Selected)` inside the BackgroundColor3, BackgroundTransparency and UIStroke `Enabled` bindings.
`cleanup(BlockPlacer.BlockTypeChanged:Connect(...))` disconnects the signal, and `cleanup(gui)` also removes the ScreenGui.
`slot(props: SlotProps)` takes BlockType, IsSelected and Select and is generated from `props.BlockTypes`, which is BlockTypes.List.
64 px slots at a minimum UIScale of 1 make a 352 px centred bar that clears the thumbstick and jump button on a 667 px-wide phone; key hints hide on touch.
Passes every check and updates the selection immediately on tap, but rewrites Main.client.luau in a new style (const, @game requires) and adds a fairly heavy Screen module.

strengths: Small, focused diff that follows the existing code style
Tile size adapts to the screen and never drops below 44 px
Signal cleanup is correct and the highlight is fully reactive
weaknesses: Slot reaches into BlockPlacer instead of taking a select callback prop
Unmounting leaves the ScreenGui in PlayerGui
Key hint visibility is read once from KeyboardEnabled

strengths: Pure, props-driven Hotbar and slot components with a Select callback
Removes the ScreenGui on unmount and updates the highlight immediately after a tap
Key hints follow the current input type through a binding
weaknesses: Unneeded style rewrite of the existing Main.client.luau
Screen module keeps module-level connections and adds complexity beyond the task
